subject.title: Feature Request: Plugin Circuit Breaker for graceful degradation

question: Should OpenClaw core own a generic plugin circuit breaker with persisted state and operator reset controls, or should circuit breaking remain plugin/channel-specific with only smaller shared telemetry seams in core?
rationale: The issue describes real stability impact, but the proposed fix changes plugin execution semantics, persistence, config, and operator workflow across all plugins.

options.title: Design core breaker contract
options.body: Create a plugin runtime/API design for hook attribution, persisted state, status output, reset commands, fail modes, and upgrade behavior before implementation.

options.title: Keep breakers plugin-owned
options.body: Narrow this to shared telemetry only, leaving active degradation policy inside each plugin or channel owner.

options.title: Phase only telemetry first
options.body: Land timing/error/lock attribution without auto-disabling hooks until budgets and compatibility behavior are proven.

recommendation.title: Design core breaker contract
recommendation.body: Create a plugin runtime/API design for hook attribution, persisted state, status output, reset commands, fail modes, and upgrade behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows repeated ownership across plugin hook timeout, session-lock stability, and gateway architecture work adjacent to this product/API decision.
